title: Create a Space sends its main heading twice in the raw HTML and is the only marketing page that is never cached

source.ref: SCAN-1032 production header sweep, 2026-11-16 (fetched through the Vercel connector; no JavaScript run).

detail: MEASURED 2026-11-16 on production: /create-a-space answers x-vercel-cache MISS with cache-control private, no-store on every fetch (the page declares force-dynamic), where the other 14 marketing pages in the audit list are prerendered and edge cached. Its h1 text also appears twice in the server HTML: once in the Suspense fallback and once in the streamed segment. WHY IT MATTERS: every visit to the main sign-up door pays a server render, and a crawler that does not run JavaScript reads two main headings. NOT YET KNOWN: whether the page must be dynamic (it redirects existing Space owners and starts the 12-minute timer for some entrants, both owner rulings of 2026-11-12), so caching it needs an owner ruling, not a blind fix. FIX DIRECTION: give the fallback a non-heading placeholder so one h1 is sent; then decide whether the per-visitor parts can move behind a client or Suspense boundary so the shell can be cached.

verify.evidence: Fails today: the production HTML of /create-a-space contains its h1 text twice and the response is private, no-store. Passes when the raw HTML carries one h1, and the caching question has a recorded owner ruling.
